summary: Jan P. Hogendijk is a historian and Indologist who studied at Utrecht University (c. 1973–1983). He held posts at Brown, Frankfurt, Heidelberg, Utrecht, Leiden, the University of Tehran, and King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals.

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann works in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Marianne Pieper and also studied under traditional teachers Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Westerhoff is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Cambridge and the University of London (including SOAS), he held positions at Durham University, Lady Margaret Hall, and the University of Oxford.

Jan Willem de Jong was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a PhD at Leiden University and studied under Paul Demiéville and Walter Eugene Clark. He held posts at Harvard, Leiden, and Australian National University.

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under David P. Jackson, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Nubpa Rinpoche. He held posts at Munich, Hamburg, Copenhagen (2003–2006), and the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project.
Jane Bunnag is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of London by 1969, where she studied under supervisors E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed her PhD at UC Berkeley (c. 1973–1981) and held appointments at Stony Brook, Amherst College, the University of Michigan, and Harvard University.

Janet R. Goodwin works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history. She studied at UC Berkeley under Delmer M. Brown and Britten Dean, and held academic posts at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu.

Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. His studies were conducted under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, as well as teachers Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances A. Wilson.

Janice Dean Willis is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religion, and Tibetology. She studied at Cornell and Columbia (PhD c. 1972–1976) under Alex Wayman and Thubten Yeshe. She was a longtime professor at Wesleyan University (c. 1977–2014).

Jann Ronis works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Virginia under David Germano, Nicolas Sihlé, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Jeffrey Hopkins, and held a post there attested in 2007.
Jared Rhoton was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Sakya Trizin and completed his dissertation at Columbia University under Alex Wayman in 1985.

Jarl Charpentier was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University and the University of Bonn under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and Hermann Jacobi. He served as an assistant professor at Uppsala University, later succeeding Johansson in 1927.

Jason Birch is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at the University of Sydney and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson and Peter Oldmeadow, later holding research posts at Oxford and SOAS University of London.

Jason Matthew McCombs specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a BS from the University of Michigan and a PhD from UCLA under Gregory Schopen, subsequently serving as a lecturer at UCLA around 2014.

Jason Neelis works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at UT Austin and the University of Washington under Richard Salomon, he held posts at Washington, Ruhr University Bochum, and Wilfrid Laurier University.
Jason Protass is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD from Stanford University under John Kieschnick, and held research positions at Academia Sinica and Ryukoku University.

Jay Holt Valentine specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delaware, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Kurtis R. Schaeffer.

Jay Jasanoff is a linguist and Indologist. After completing his studies at Harvard University (c. 1963–1968), he held academic posts at UC Berkeley, Cornell University (c. 1978–1998), and Harvard University from around 1998.

Jay L. Garfield is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He has held faculty posts at Hampshire College, Smith College, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the University of Massachusetts Amherst, the University of Melbourne, and NUS.
